subject: Cortex Solutions — Embedder discovery recap & milestone plan
messages:
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cortexsolutions.com>, Dana Rivera <dana.rivera@cortexsolutions.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Cortex discovery — quick recap + next milestones

Alex / Dana,

Thanks again for the call today — really constructive. I wanted to capture the key pain points we heard, summarize how Redwood could help, and propose a short milestone plan so we can get a technical kickoff scheduled next week.

What we heard (priority order):
- Search relevance: current semantic embeddings + ranking pipeline degrades for short queries (2–6 tokens). Re-rank layer is a manual ruleset that is expensive to maintain.
- Latency sensitivity: sub-100ms P95 on ranking endpoint for UI flows is critical for adoption.
- Streaming & structured output: product team needs token-level streaming for multi-part responses, and a strict JSON schema (structured output) for downstream parsing.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence and audit log access required before pilot.

How Redwood maps to those needs (high level):
- Embeddings + reranking: we recommend a hybrid setup — on-device prefilter + Redwood-hosted advanced embeddings and a rerank model for the top-K. This reduces per-request tokens and keeps cost close to current spend.
- Streaming + function-calls: Redwood supports streaming token-by-token and our function-calling primitives to emit validated JSON objects (structured output) to your service hooks.
- Latency controls: dedicated capacity option and workload-aware batching give predictable P95; we can reserve capacity for your top traffic routes.
- Compliance: we will share SOC2 and provide audit log hooks for the pilot.

Proposed immediate milestones (attached spreadsheet has timelines):
1) Technical deep-dive (1.5h) — product + infra engineers (week of Sep 6) — owner: Ben Carter (redwood) / Alex (cortex)
2) Security questionnaire & data flow diagram — owner: Dana (cortex) / Marissa (redwood) — deliverable: completed questionnaire (Sep 10)
3) Pilot config & PKI for private traffic (if needed) — owner: Redwood infra — target Sep 17
4) Pilot run (2 weeks) with metrics: P95 latency, top-K accuracy delta, cost per query — target Sep 20

Next steps from my side: I’ll put Ben on a short technical thread and share the high-level M.A.P. (attached). Can you confirm availability for the deep-dive (Ben suggested Tue/Thu morning PST)?

Cheers,
Ethan Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0194

Thanks Ethan — this is perfect and captures the call well. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- The ranking endpoint target is 80–100ms median, 120ms P95 for requester-facing calls. The 100ms P95 you called out is acceptable as a ceiling for the pilot but we will need to tighten in production.
- Our rerank currently runs on batches of 50 candidates; we are open to a top-10 rerank after a lightweight prefilter. Cost per query is a major gating criterion.
- Streaming is a must for our agent UI (we cannot buffer full responses before display). The structured JSON must conform to our interactions schema (I attached interaction-schema.json to the internal drive link).

Dana and I are available for the technical deep-dive on Tue morning PST (Sep 7) or Thu morning PST (Sep 9). Either works for engineering.

One ask: can Ben include a short note in the tech kickoff that describes the KV-cache behavior and how Redwood's prefix-caching could reduce repeated token costs? That'll help our infra folks reason about cost allocation.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alex

Subject: Re: Cortex discovery — technical kickoff agenda + KV-cache note

Alex / team — thanks, happy to join the deep-dive. Two quick pre-read notes so we can make the 1.5h session actionable: 

1) KV cache & prefix caching
- Redwood's KV cache stores per-session KV for autoregressive decoding; for rerank use cases we recommend a short-lived prefix cache for identical context fragments (e.g., user metadata + static prompt). This reduces token recomputation for repeated short queries and can cut token costs by ~25% for high-repeat traffic.

2) Streaming + structured output
- Our streaming supports early partial JSON emission and a final commit event. For safety we can validate the structured payload on the server side and emit a 'validation' event over the stream so your UI can fall back to a sanitized version if schema validation fails.

3) Proposed agenda for the deep-dive (1.5h):
- 0:00–0:15: introductions & success metrics (Cortex leads)
- 0:15–0:40: current pipeline walkthrough (Cortex) + data shapes
- 0:40–1:05: Redwood architecture — embedding + rerank options, quantization & perf notes
- 1:05–1:20: integration patterns — streaming, function-calls, structured output, webhook plumbing
- 1:20–1:30: next steps & action owners (capture in mutual action plan)

Action items I’ll take before the call:
- Share a 2-page tech note on quantized model tradeoffs and recommended model sizes for your latency targets (attached: redwood-internal-tech-notes.pdf).
- Prep a sample structured-output function-call example for your interaction-schema (we'll post to the shared drive).

I’ll block Tue Sep 7 09:00–10:30 PST as a tentative slot. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite with dial-in and a short pre-read.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
